android_mechanism: List rows are re-created during scrolling instead of being recycled
bug_description: The browsing-history dialog renders each day's entries with a plain ForEach inside ListItemGroup, so when the dialog opens, HistoryItem components for every recorded entry (including off-screen ones) are created eagerly, and scrolling re-creates components instead of recycling them. Opening the history dialog and scrolling it is slow once history grows.
fix_summary: History entries are rendered with LazyForEach backed by a per-group IDataSource implementation, so row components are created on demand as they enter the viewport and recycled while scrolling.
trigger_steps: Seed the app with a large history (browse ~100 pages in one day).
Start hitrace capture (categories: ace, app, sched).
Open the pages/history dialog (bottom bar history button) and scroll the list from top to bottom at constant speed.
Stop hitrace. Repeat 3 repetitions for unfixed, then install the fixed HAP and repeat 3 repetitions.

test_oracle.definition: (a) Time from dialog-open event to first rendered history frame; (b) count of HistoryItem component build/attach operations in the ace trace during the whole scroll; (c) dropped-frame count while scrolling.
test_oracle.comparison: unfixed builds all N components at open (N = seeded entries) vs fixed builds only visible rows (~10-15); unfixed_first_frame_ms > fixed_first_frame_ms; unfixed shows more jank frames during scroll.

trace_config.command: hdc shell hitrace --time 20 ace app sched graphic -o /data/local/tmp/browser_histlist.chtrace
